coding.note: The report describes released KOSMOS-2.5 and KOSMOS-2.5-CHAT models. No controlled ablations or independent-run counts are reported. Data disclosure is conservatively PARTIAL: Table 2 supplies category sampling ratios and several named sources, but broad web-crawled PDF/DOCX/design/project collections are not specified sufficiently to reconstruct them. Comparator evaluation provenance and copied-score provenance are not explicitly stated, so both are NR; new benchmarks alone do not establish a common evaluation harness for all reported comparators. Comparators are capped at 15, prioritizing Table 8 and adding GPT-4o and Vary from the reading tables. The existing encoder, resampler, coordinate-token approach, and autoregressive objective are attributed to prior work; no explicit renaming is identified.

claims.claim: Two complementary document-reading pre-training tasks learn document order and structure: document-level text recognition and image-to-markdown generation.
claims.quote:
We propose two distinct yet cooperative document read-
  ing tasks for pre-training a foundational document model
  capable of machine reading and understanding the order
  and structure of text-intensive documents.

claims.claim: A shared decoder-only autoregressive Transformer with task-specific prompts unifies spatially-aware and markdown transcription.
claims.quote:
This unified multimodal literate capability is achieved
  through a shared decoder-only autoregressive Transformer
architecture and task-specific prompts.

claims.claim: Fine-tuning the pre-trained model yields the document-understanding generalist KOSMOS-2.5-CHAT with competitive performance at 1.3B parameters.
claims.quote:
Building on this foun-
  dation, we fine-tune KOSMOS -2.5 for document understand-
  ing tasks, resulting in a document understanding generalist
  named KOSMOS -2.5- CHAT.

claims.claim: A large, diverse corpus of 357.4 million document images annotated with bounding boxes or markdown is curated for pre-training.
claims.quote:
We curated a large and diverse corpus consisting of 357.4
  million text-rich document images, with text lines anno-
  tated with bounding boxes or in markdown format.

claims.claim: An automated data collection, filtering, and quality-control pipeline provides insights for future document-reading research.
claims.quote:
The automated data curation pipeline provides valuable in-
  sights for future research.

claims.claim: Two comprehensive benchmarks, OCREval and MarkdownEval, evaluate document-level text recognition and image-to-markdown generation across diverse domains.
claims.quote:
We introduce two comprehensive benchmarks, OCREval
  and MarkdownEval, to provide thorough evaluations of
  document-level machine reading capabilities.

data_disclosure.quote:
our pre-training dataset encompasses a
  wide range of document types, including scanned documents,
  academic papers, web pages, design images, mathematical
  content, handwritten text, and more.

tokens_disclosed.quote:
The total training
involved approximately 260 billion tokens.
